spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Odd Gaussian subordination produces a symmetric extremal pair for f. Parity collapses the two-sided verification, and a sinc-squared correction isolates the entire L1 discrepancy, giving equal error pi/(2 Delta).

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit represents an odd scaled kernel H_Delta as a mixture of odd Gaussians with a claimed finite nonnegative measure, invokes unique extremals M_Delta^-/M_Delta^+, and gives interpolation formulas related by M_Delta^-(z)=-M_Delta^+(-z). It proves growth and real-axis bounds from series for f and f', rescales to m_Delta^+/- for f, identifies an odd part plus a sinc-squared correction, computes the L1 error, and obtains Fourier support by Paley-Wiener.
directed.conceptual_reading: Oddness is functional leverage, not just symmetry: it makes one extremal determine the other and makes the integrated odd component cancel, leaving a universal correction term as the exact approximation cost.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge runs from f to H_Delta, then to an odd-Gaussian measure and interpolation extremals; the sinc-squared term connects parity to exact L1 error.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The needed positivity and finiteness of the subordinating measure are deferred to the appendix, so the construction in this span depends on that unproved condition.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate: the parity and error mechanism are clear, while the measure and interpolation formulas are sensitive to extraction.

supported: The span states the odd-Gaussian mixture with positivity and finiteness deferred to Appendix A, invokes cited unique extremals, gives their interpolation formulas and parity relation, and proves growth and real-axis bounds before reaching the decomposition into an odd term J_Delta plus a sinc-squared correction.
inference: Oddness making one extremal determine the other is directly supported, and anticipating that the odd term will integrate to zero is a reasonable next-step inference.
unsupported_or_imported: The exact L1 error pi/(2 Delta) and compact Fourier support are not proved in this artifact; both computations occur at the start of the next assigned span and are imported here across the unit boundary.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The symmetry discussion is substantive, but 'universal correction term as the exact approximation cost' prematurely packages a calculation absent from this span.
context_or_ocr_risk: The unit begins with the tail of the preceding even-extremal calculation and ends immediately after setting up parts (ii) and (iii); measure normalizations are formula-sensitive.
missed_mechanism: Within this boundary the sinc-squared term is only isolated, not yet integrated, and Paley-Wiener has not yet been applied to the odd extremals.
revision_instructions: Stop the source-grounded account at the parity, bounds and J_Delta-plus-sinc decomposition; label exact error and Fourier support as deferred to the following span.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The deferred Gaussian representation is reduced to elementary integral transforms: Fubini and a reciprocal change of variables evaluate the inner Gaussian integral, while positivity of the measure density is reduced to a one-parameter monotonicity-style integral involving sin y-y cos y.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The appendix writes H_Delta(x) as a double integral, changes variables, evaluates a bracketed lambda-integral as exp(-xy/Delta) using k to 1/k symmetry and a Gaussian change of variables, and thereby proves the representation. It then rescales the proposed density D(Delta,lambda) and reduces nonnegativity to showing an integral of exp(-y^2/(4a^2))(sin y-y cos y) is nonnegative; the artifact ends as integration by parts and an odd-Gaussian Fourier transform are applied.
directed.conceptual_reading: The certification separates identity from order: transform manipulations prove that the measure represents the target, while a distinct scalar inequality must prove the measure is nonnegative and hence that order survives subordination.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The double integral and evaluated kernel exp(-xy/Delta) bridge the odd target to Gaussian atoms; scaling reduces all positivity checks to a dimensionless parameter a.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The available span stops mid-positivity calculation and does not visibly complete nonnegativity or finite-total-mass verification, despite those being the appendix's announced purpose. Those conclusions should not be reconstructed here.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate: the representation proof is complete in the span, but the decisive positivity certification is truncated and transform normalizations are formula-sensitive.

supported: The opening lines compute the exact L1 error from oddness and the sinc-squared correction and obtain Fourier support via Paley-Wiener; Appendix A then proves the integral representation of H_Delta and reduces nonnegativity of the proposed measure to a one-parameter Gaussian-weighted sine inequality.
inference: Separating representation identity from positivity/order certification is a strong and source-faithful conceptual reading of the appendix.
unsupported_or_imported: The analysis does not falsely claim completion of the positivity or finite-mass proof, but it omits the fully supported L1-error and Fourier-support results actually contained at the top of this span.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The transform-bridge language is specific to the k-to-1/k symmetry, Gaussian change of variables and resulting exp(-xy/Delta) kernel.
context_or_ocr_risk: The unit starts by completing Lemma 8 from the preceding span and ends mid-positivity calculation; transform normalizations are formula-sensitive.
missed_mechanism: This span, not the preceding one, closes the exact-error and compact-support obligations for the odd extremals before beginning the deferred measure certification.
revision_instructions: Add the exact L1 and Paley-Wiener support conclusions as source facts, then retain the representation proof and clearly mark positivity and finite mass as unfinished at the boundary.
